messages:
nora: FYI saw a morning spike in fncall rejects from retail-ingest. console shows hard errors but responses are arrays vs expected object. looks like strict validator canary flipped and routed to degen, product thinks requests are failing.
mike: paste an example?
sasha: reminder: we rolled stricter fncall validator as a canary in eu-west at 02:00. fallback to cheaper variant is enabled.
nora: example log line:
``
validator:{"error":"invalid_shape","details":"expected object, got array","sample":"[{\"id\":123,\"text\":\"ok\"}]"}
``
The call returned useful content; adapter expects {items: []} so we mark fncall rejected, route to degen, and console increments error.
albert: that explains the dashboard spike. product saw SLA regression and opened a ticket.
janet: billing question: which route gets charged when we fall back?
mike: billing uses final_model_id for charge. the 'validation_reject' metric is incremented on origin route (canonical route) and that's what console surfaces as an error. mismatch is confusing.
sasha: telemetry fix: add tags fallback_reason, origin_route_id, final_model_id, counted_for_billing to every fallback event.
janet: +1. product also wants a redacted sample in console popover for triage.
albert: ops idea: page if soft-fallback rate >5% in 15m with top samples; otherwise it stays a metric.
nora: two UX proposals: A) console show "soft-fallback" (amber) with origin + charge info B) don't count harmless array/object coercions as hard validation_rejects; mark them as soft-coerce.
mike: add per-route config: treat_fncall_shape_mismatch_as = [reject|soft|coerce]. default enterprise='soft'. surface setting in console.
sasha: impl notes: validator should emit reason codes and coercion_suggestion when possible; adapters can optionally wrap array -> {items: array} if route allows coercion.
janet: product timeline: console + telemetry tags in 2 sprints; billing policy and per-route knob in 3 sprints.
albert: rollout nuance: auto-flip currently uses strict-validate rejects to trigger traffic moves to degen. we should exclude 'soft' reasons from auto-flip.
mike: agree. auto-flip should only consider fatal rejects and capacity fallbacks.
janet: also update billing docs with exact behavior and show it in the console popover.
sasha: action items:
- S1 telemetry: add tags (sasha)
- S1 console: add soft-fallback state + popover + sample (janet)
- S2 validator: reason codes + coercion_suggestion (mike)
- S2 adapters: optional coercion wrapper + per-route opt-in (albert)
- S2 billing: draft policy for soft-coerces (janet + finance)
- S3 rollout: exclude soft reasons from auto-flip (mike)
sasha: I'll open tickets and land telemetry schema changes.
janet: I'll update console mocks and product notes; will route billing language to legal.
mike: adding monitoring alert rule 5%/15m for soft-fallback rate (owner: eng-oncall).
deploy-bot: deploy 1716000200-fncall-validator-v2 -> succeeded (canary eu-west)
nora: thanks. if anyone sees >10% soft-fallback on a route before we ship, @ops and paste top 3 samples here. :thumbsup:
